dedupe_keys.name: resilience of food sufficiency to future climate and societal changes global caloric sufficiency scenarios to 2050

description: This data set asks whether the world will grow enough calories to feed its population by 2050 once climate change and crop adaptation are taken into account, country by country. The producers are Charlotte Weil, Justin Johnson and Romain Caristan, who released the data with notebooks in a public GitHub repository. Coverage is global and national, across five scenarios of climate and societal change in which farmers switch crop mixes to suit new conditions. The central finding is that global caloric sufficiency is likely to fall even though production rises, because population grows faster, and that most countries facing hunger today remain vulnerable. The archive, about 14 gigabytes, is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and the repository explains how to set up the Python environment and rerun the analysis; the record asks users to take version 2. Caveats: sufficiency measures calories only, not trade, access or nutrition, and results depend on the chosen crop and climate models. Simulation uses: setting national food supply stress under climate scenarios for resilience models of food distribution and emergency food reserves. Related records: the global food security projections database (data-global-food-security-projections-database) compares many such projections, and FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give today's supply.
